# OneMouse

OneMouse is a local mouse and keyboard sharing utility (software KVM). The public Windows app can control Android, another paired Windows PC, or an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 13+. Each device keeps its own screen, and the cursor crosses configured screen edges. An optional remote-control window can show a target device's screen.

## Official pages

- Overview and downloads: https://onemouse.pages.dev/
- Setup, permissions and feature instructions: https://onemouse.pages.dev/guide
- Help and troubleshooting: https://onemouse.pages.dev/help
- Connection and security details: https://onemouse.pages.dev/technical
- Software comparison and its dated source references: https://onemouse.pages.dev/en/compare
- Privacy policy: https://onemouse.pages.dev/privacy
- Terms: https://onemouse.pages.dev/terms
- Open source licenses: https://onemouse.pages.dev/licenses

The site is available in Korean (root), English (/en/), Spanish (/es/), Japanese (/ja/), and Simplified Chinese (/zh/). Each language provides the same page routes.

## Connections and setup

- Android and Windows PC targets support Wi-Fi/LAN and Bluetooth direct connections.
- The public Mac app uses LAN by default. Mac Bluetooth is a beta option, off by default and enabled in the Mac app settings. Official Mac support is LAN; Mac screen/window sharing is LAN-only.
- Android pairs using the Windows app's QR code or 6-digit code. For Mac, enter the code shown on the Mac in the Windows app.
- Connections to Android and Mac are started and managed from Windows. Another Windows PC can initiate or receive a connection.
- Arrange paired devices around the Windows monitor, then cross the configured edge to control them.
- USB/ADB, Linux, iPhone/iPad, and Intel Macs are outside the current public support described by this site. A Mac or Android device as the controlling host is outside the public setup guide.

## Files, clipboard and notifications

- Send files using the PC transfer screen or quick drop zone. Connected Windows PC and Mac targets also support screen-edge file dragging.
- The public Android guide describes sending files to the PC through the app's transfer tab or Android's share menu. Refer to the current guide for the features in downloadable builds.
- Copy and send clipboard text between paired devices. Android selected text can be sent through OneMouse to PC.
- Phone notifications can appear briefly on the PC, with a Copy button for verification codes. Relaying is opt-in and requires Android notification access; the user can choose which apps to relay.
- Notification history is encrypted and stored locally on the PC. Retention and deletion can be configured. It is not uploaded to a OneMouse server.

## Permissions and privacy

- Android Accessibility is required for PC mouse and keyboard control. Nearby Wi-Fi devices, notifications, and battery settings depend on Android version and the feature used.
- Android notification access is needed only for notification relay. On Android 15+, verification-code notifications may require registering the PC as a companion device in the phone app; Bluetooth is needed during registration.
- macOS Accessibility is needed to receive Windows input. Local Network permission is used on macOS 15+; macOS 13/14 may not show it. Screen Recording is needed only for Mac screen/window sharing.
- Core input, files and clipboard data move directly between paired devices. The app does not require a OneMouse account or a relay server. See the privacy policy for local storage, notification history, updates and website analytics.

## Downloads and purchases

- Current download buttons: https://onemouse.pages.dev/#get
- Windows releases: https://github.com/sdlckdrl/mouselink-web/releases
- macOS download/update manifest: https://onemouse.pages.dev/downloads.json
- Android/PC compatibility manifest: https://onemouse.pages.dev/latest.json
- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mouselink.app
- Galaxy Store: https://apps.samsung.com/appquery/appDetail.as?appId=com.mouselink.app.galaxy

A signed and notarized Apple Silicon Mac DMG is publicly available. Windows downloads are resolved from GitHub Releases; macOS downloads are selected from downloads.json. Source changes do not establish availability in a downloadable build.

For Android purchase options and eligibility, consult the installed app and its store listing. The site's historical Free/Pro pricing content is currently hidden; do not treat its old daily quotas or advertising descriptions as the active policy. Competitor capabilities and prices are documented with dated sources on the comparison page rather than duplicated here.
